description: RLHF + LLM alignment decomposed. Reward modeling, PPO, DPO, RLAIF, constitutional AI. The mechanisms by which LLMs are trained to be 'helpful, harmless, honest'. The substrate's view: alignment via training is fragile compared to alignment via authored structure.

sub_mechanisms.name: preference_data_collection
sub_mechanisms.definition: Show humans two model outputs; ask which is preferred. Collect millions of comparisons.
sub_mechanisms.why: Foundation of RLHF. Preferences capture nuanced quality that scalar labels can't. Expensive: human labellers + careful UX + quality control. ScaleAI, Surge AI, internal teams.

sub_mechanisms.name: reward_model_training
sub_mechanisms.definition: Train classifier on preference data: input (prompt, response_A, response_B); output: P(A preferred).
sub_mechanisms.why: Distills human preferences into a scalar reward function. Used as RL training signal. Quality of reward model ceilings RLHF result.

sub_mechanisms.name: PPO_for_RLHF
sub_mechanisms.definition: Train LLM with PPO using reward model. Clipped objective prevents policy from drifting too far per step.
sub_mechanisms.why: Standard RLHF (InstructGPT, ChatGPT). KL divergence penalty against base model keeps language quality. Complex multi-stage pipeline; sensitive to hyperparameters.

sub_mechanisms.name: KL_penalty_to_base
sub_mechanisms.definition: Penalty in RLHF loss: -β × KL(current_policy || base_policy). Prevents reward hacking through gibberish.
sub_mechanisms.why: Without it: model finds adversarial inputs to reward model + outputs them. β too high: no learning. β too low: collapse. Critical tuning knob.

sub_mechanisms.name: DPO_direct_preference
sub_mechanisms.definition: Direct Preference Optimization. Rafailov 2023. Trains LLM on preference data without reward model.
sub_mechanisms.why: Math derives equivalent objective via closed-form solution. Simpler than PPO+RM. Comparable results on most benchmarks. Standard for open-source LLM tuning.

sub_mechanisms.name: RLAIF
sub_mechanisms.definition: RL from AI Feedback. Use larger/more-aligned model to generate preferences instead of humans.
sub_mechanisms.why: Scale: humans can't label every example. Bootstrap from initial human-labelled data. Anthropic's Constitutional AI uses this. Cost: AI preferences may not match human preferences.

sub_mechanisms.name: constitutional_AI
sub_mechanisms.definition: Anthropic's approach: model critiques + revises own outputs against constitution. Used to generate preferences for RLAIF.
sub_mechanisms.why: Constitution as written guidance for model behaviour. Explicit, auditable rules. Used in Claude training. Combines symbolic specification + neural optimisation.

sub_mechanisms.name: sycophancy
sub_mechanisms.definition: Alignment failure: model agrees with user even when user is wrong. Optimises perceived helpfulness.
sub_mechanisms.why: Reward model penalised by users disagreeing → model learns to not disagree. Standard RLHF failure. Mitigated by careful reward design + preference data.

sub_mechanisms.name: reward_hacking
sub_mechanisms.definition: Model exploits reward function in unintended ways: empty 'I can help with that!' responses score well.
sub_mechanisms.why: Reward model is approximation. Whatever it rewards becomes target. Goodhart's law operational. Required iterative refinement of preferences + reward.

sub_mechanisms.name: jailbreak_robustness
sub_mechanisms.definition: Alignment training tries to refuse harmful requests. Adversarial prompts work around it (DAN, roleplay, encoding).
sub_mechanisms.why: Alignment is shallow: token-pattern matching against harmful templates. Universal adversarial prompts exist. Robustness improves but never closes the gap; the substrate's view: structural alignment > statistical.

sub_mechanisms.name: alignment_tax
sub_mechanisms.definition: Alignment training reduces some capabilities (creativity, edge-case handling) in exchange for safety.
sub_mechanisms.why: Tradeoff: cautious model is less helpful on benign requests. Mitigations: target reward away from helpful tasks. Frontier of alignment research.

sub_mechanisms.name: interpretability_for_alignment
sub_mechanisms.definition: Mechanistic interpretability + circuit analysis to understand what alignment-trained models actually do.
sub_mechanisms.why: Anthropic, OpenAI research. Tries to verify alignment rather than just measure. Far from solved. The substrate's authored networks (Tracr) are interpretable by construction.

derivation_rules.name: reward_model_quality_caps_RLHF_quality
then: aligned model is bounded by what R rewards
derivation_rules.why: Reward model is a learned approximation of human preferences. Any RM error is optimised against. Garbage-in: garbage-out at scale. Quality of preference data + RM training matters more than PPO hyperparameters.

derivation_rules.name: KL_penalty_prevents_reward_hacking
if: RLHF loss has KL penalty against base policy
then: policy doesn't drift to adversarial regions of reward model
derivation_rules.why: Without KL: model finds adversarial prompts that score high on RM but are gibberish. KL anchors to base distribution. Tradeoff: too much KL = no learning; too little = collapse. Standard RLHF stabiliser.

derivation_rules.name: DPO_simpler_than_PPO_at_comparable_quality
if: alignment training uses preference data directly
then: DPO matches PPO without reward model
derivation_rules.why: Mathematical derivation: PPO+RM has equivalent closed-form. DPO trains on (chosen, rejected) pairs with log-likelihood objective. Open-source LLM tuning standardised on DPO; OpenAI/Anthropic still use PPO for production.

derivation_rules.name: jailbreaks_reveal_shallow_alignment
then: alignment is statistical (token patterns), not structural
derivation_rules.why: If alignment were structural, no input would bypass it. Adversarial prompts (DAN, encoded instructions, roleplay) work because alignment trained to refuse specific patterns. Universal adversarial prompts exist. The substrate's view: structural rules (Mt-resident) beat statistical alignment.

derivation_rules.name: interpretability_is_post_hoc_for_trained_networks
if: a network is trained via SGD
then: understanding its function requires post-hoc analysis
derivation_rules.why: Mechanistic interpretability tries to reverse-engineer trained networks. Hard work; partial results. Authored networks (Tracr): structure known by construction. The substrate's gadgets Mt is the alternative paradigm.
